AbstractText.Label: CONTEXT
AbstractText.content: The rate of live discharge from hospice and the proportion of hospices exceeding their aggregate caps have both steadily increased for the last 15 years, becoming a source of federal scrutiny. The cap restricts aggregate payments hospices receive from Medicare during a 12-month period. The risk of repayment and the manner in which the cap is calculated may incentivize hospices coming close to their cap ceilings to discharge existing patients prior to the end of the cap year.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The objective of this work was to explore annual cap-risk trends and live discharge patterns. We hypothesized that as a hospice comes closer to exceeding its cap, a patient's likelihood of being discharged alive increases.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We analyzed monthly hospice outcomes using 2012-13 Medicare claims.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Adjusted analyses showed a positive and statistically significant relationship between cap risk and live discharges.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Policymakers ought to consider the unintended consequences the aggregate cap may be having on patient outcomes of care.
